original.target_description: Experiment 1a: moral acceptability ratings, footbridge switch versus footbridge pole, covariate-adjusted planned personal-force contrast.

n.quote: The footbridge pole dilemma (n = 72, Fig. 1b) is identical to the standard footbridge dilemma except that Joe uses a pole rather than his hands to push the victim.
n.sample_role: Participants in the footbridge pole versus footbridge switch contrast; analytic n for the covariate-adjusted test cannot be established from the printed report.
n.exclusions: PDF p. 3 excludes 31 of 664 conscious realists and 10 reporting confusion. Printed condition counts are pole 72 and switch 160; the model includes realism covariates and gender. Post-exclusion complete-case counts for this contrast are not separately printed.

es.location: PDF p. 4, section 2.2 Results, personal-force planned contrast

replication.target_description: Study 1: Canadian undergraduates, footbridge switch versus footbridge pole moral acceptability ratings; Welch independent t-test.

n.sample_role: Participants in two mutually exclusive final between-subjects groups in the target Welch independent t-test.
n.exclusions: Analysis Plan excludes those confused (N = 7) or lacking realism (N = 11); these study-wide counts are not allocated to target groups. Final target group counts are given directly in Table 2.
n.location: Table 2, canonical page 15, Footbridge Pole versus Footbridge Switch; Table 1 study design; Analysis Plan, canonical page 7.

p.quote: force for the footbridge dilemmas (footbridge switch vs. footbridge pole; p = .02, d = -.37).

reported_success.quote: We found that personal force influences a person’s decision in footbridge and speedboat dilemmas, such that a person is more likely to present a deontological response if the action entails personal force, supporting H1 and H2.

notes:
Original and replication titles verified against supplied references. Original analytic contrast sample is not securely established; printed condition sizes are retained only as context. Replication uses a within-subject footbridge/speedboat component but each personal-force comparison is between groups. Author verdict is successful for the assigned personal-force hypothesis; authors describe their overall replication as partial.
